newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves US$11.31 mln in China investments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves US$11.31 mln in China investments.

text.p: Taiwan's Economics Ministry has given the nod to 10 China-bound investment projects worth US$11.31 million, a statement said on Monday.
The ministry agreed to let Charoen Pokphand Enterprises invest $1.08 million in a food processing venture in the mainland.
It did not give details of the rest of the projects, which were conducted by unlisted firms, but said they involved only small amounts of money and low technology.

Worried that the island may become over-dependent on the mainland for investment, President Lee Teng-hui said in August that the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market.

Taiwan officials, including Lee, have repeatedly accused China of using commerce as a political lever against the island and told local businessmen that it was time to slow their investment projects in the mainland.

Though all investments in China must be government approved and routed indirectly through Hong Kong or other third places, Taiwan remains concerned that its economy may become too dependent on China -- and hence politically vulnerable.
Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with China since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Despite the ban, indirect commerce has flourished since the late 1980s when political tensions started to thaw. Some 30,000 Taiwan companies have poured more than US$20 billion into China so far.
